Roofing in Haltom City, Texas

Haltom City keeps a roofing permit form of its own, and a roofer has to be registered with the city to get one. Call one free number any hour to reach an independent roofing company that takes Haltom City calls.

Call (469) 649-7066 The Haltom City roof permit

  2. Service Areas
  3. Haltom City

Haltom Village grew up next door to Fort Worth

Roofing in Haltom City, TX means working on one of the older suburbs in northeast Tarrant County. The city's own history traces Haltom Village to 1932, when it was founded on ranch and farm land and named for G. W. Haltom, a Fort Worth jeweler.

Growth came from the Meadow Oaks development and from new highways that made the drive to Fort Worth, the rest of northeast Tarrant County and Dallas easier. Those state highways were routed past the old Birdville business district in 1932. The result today is a mix of long-settled residential streets and busy commercial corridors, with plenty of roofs that have been replaced more than once.

DFW Expert Roofers does not work on any of them; think of it as a free switchboard. A recorded voice assistant picks up, hears out the problem with your roof, and patches the call through to an independent, locally owned roofing company serving Haltom City. Inspection, estimate, labor and the bill all belong to that company.

What the Haltom City roofing permit asks for

Haltom City keeps a dedicated Residential Roofing Permit application, plus a contractor registration form. Between them, they tell you what the city wants to see.

The materials

The permit form asks for the type of shingle, the type of felt and the thickness of the decking. Ask your roofer to put the same three items in your contract so the two match.

A registered roofer

All contractors must register with the city to receive permits. The registration form asks for a driver's license and a certificate of insurance naming Haltom City as the certificate holder.

A start date

The permit becomes invalid if the work it covers does not start within 180 days. The fee notes also list a higher charge when work begins without a permit.

Applications go through the city's online portal. Planning and Inspections is at City Hall, 4801 Haltom Road, and the department has listed weekday hours Monday through Thursday. Confirm current requirements with the city before work starts.

Older homes bring worn shingles and leaks around vents and chimneys, and the commercial roads bring low-slope roofs over shops. These pages cover each.

When the city sends a storm warning

Haltom City passes National Weather Service warnings along to residents through its Nixle alerts. A warning relayed in late August 2026 called for gusts to 60 mph and hail the size of quarters, and it told people to expect wind damage to roofs, siding and trees. That is a typical North Texas warm-season storm, and it is enough to loosen tabs on an older roof.

After a storm passes, stay on the ground. Walk the yard for pieces of shingle or vent caps, look at ceilings inside for new stains, and take dated photos of both. Then call your insurance company to ask how wind and hail claims work on your policy, and call a roofer.

Leave the roof to the roofer. A wet or storm-hit roof is slippery, and damaged decking can give way, so keep off it and keep the ladder put away. Stay clear of any downed power line and report it to Oncor or your local electric utility, or call 911. Inside, pull furniture and electronics away from the drip, set out a bucket or towels, and keep everyone out of a room where the ceiling is sagging. Take photos from the yard and from inside, then call your insurance company and a roofer.

Why people in Haltom City use the line

  • A roof that has been patched before. On a house that has seen several roofs, a roofer may find old layers or tired decking. The city's form asks about decking for that reason.
  • Paperwork the city checks. Registration with insurance on file and a permit with named materials give you a record of who did the work.
  • Shops as well as homes. The same number reaches a roofing company for a drip above a bed or above a cash register.
  • No hours to wait for. The assistant answers any time. If the roofer cannot pick up, it receives your name, number, need and urgency to call you back.

Questions for the roofer

  • Under what name are you registered with Haltom City, and when will you file the roofing permit?
  • Which shingle and felt will you list on the permit, and will my contract name the same ones?
  • How thick is my decking, and how will rotten sheets be priced and shown to me?
  • Will your insurer send me a liability certificate directly?

No state license for roofers. Texas does not license roofing contractors. A 2025 bill that would have had the state license re-roofers (HB 3344) cleared a House committee but never got a floor vote, and it died when the session ended. That puts the checking on you: ask for a certificate of liability insurance sent to you by the roofer's insurance agent or insurer, a written contract that lists the full scope, the permit or contractor registration your city requires, addresses of nearby jobs, and proof the shingle warranty was registered. The line does none of this checking for you. How to check a roofer in Texas.

Your deductible is yours to pay. The Texas Department of Insurance warns that a contractor may not waive your deductible, rebate it, or pad the estimate to cover it, and that a contract of $1,000 or more paid with insurance money must include a notice that you owe the deductible. Your insurer may ask for proof you paid it. A contractor also may not act as a public adjuster on a property it works on or may work on. If a roofer offers to "take care of" the deductible, hire someone else.

How a call from Haltom City works

  1. Dial the lineAn automated assistant picks up (469) 649-7066 any time and asks what you need. The same number also takes air conditioning, heating and pressure washing calls, so say "roof".
  2. Tell it about the roofHail, a drip in the ceiling, shingles in the yard, a tree limb, or an aging roof you want checked, plus your town and how soon you need someone.
  3. Get transferredThe call goes to an independent roofing company that is locally owned and works in Dallas-Fort Worth. It hears a quick summary of your call before it answers.
  4. Work with that companyIt inspects, prices and does the job, and you pay it (or your insurer does, as you arrange). If it cannot pick up, it gets your name, number, town and need so it can call you back.

Haltom City roofing questions

Do I need a roof permit in Haltom City?

Plan on it. Haltom City publishes a Residential Roofing Permit application, and its fee notes list a higher charge for work started without a permit. The form asks for the shingle type, the felt type and the decking thickness, and the permit lapses if work does not begin within 180 days of issue. Planning and Inspections at City Hall, 4801 Haltom Road, can tell you exactly what your job needs.

Does my roofer have to be registered with Haltom City?

Yes, to get a permit. The city's FAQ says all contractors must be registered with Haltom City to receive permits. Registration asks for a driver's license and a certificate of insurance that names the city as certificate holder, and the form has a category for roofing. The only exemption is a homeowner working on a homestead-exempt house they live in, with a matching driver's license.

How long does a Haltom City roof permit take?

The city's Planning and Inspection FAQ has given a processing time of about 7 to 10 business days for permits submitted through its online portal, though an older version gave a longer estimate. Ask the roofer when it will apply and to send you the permit number once it is issued. For a leak that cannot wait, ask about a temporary cover; our emergency roof repair page explains that step.

What should I check before hiring a roofer in Haltom City?

Start with the city: ask the roofer for the name on its Haltom City registration and confirm a permit will be filed. Then ask for a liability insurance certificate from its insurer, a written scope naming the shingles and felt, and a price per sheet for decking. With no state roofing license in Texas, these papers carry the weight. The roofer checklist guide goes further.
